decisions.reason: As a flagship service close to core vessel-management capabilities in an expanding firm, it is likely at or near aspiration and buffered by strategic commitment and organisational slack despite offshore-market uncertainty.
Because it builds directly on existing crew and corporate-support resources and can be bundled cheaply with core services, management would keep it unless performance clearly falls below aspiration.
As a flagship digital offering that broadens the firm’s narrow portfolio and strengthens customer proximity, it is likely retained while results mature under the firm’s available slack.
A standalone mobile performance app is more peripheral and easier to absorb into other services, so if uptake has stayed below aspiration management would redeploy resources and discontinue it.
